Poliovirus containment 
 
GUIDANCE TO MINIMIZE RISKS FOR FACILITIES 
COLLECTING, HANDLING OR STORING MATERIALS 
POTENTIALLY INFECTIOUS FOR POLIOVIRUSES, 
SECOND EDITION 
 
 
 
 
WEB ANNEX A 
COUNTRY- AND AREA-SPECIFIC POLIOVIRUS DATA, 
APRIL 2023 UPDATE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Poliovirus containment: guidance to minimize risks for facilities collecting, handling or storing materials potentially 
infectious for polioviruses, second edition. Web Annex A. Country- and area-specific poliovirus data, April 2023 update 
WHO/POLIO/23.02 
© World Health Organization 2023

summary.text: The front matter of Web Annex A to WHO's poliovirus containment guidance, which gives country- and area-specific poliovirus data as of April 2023 (WHO/POLIO/23.02). It contains the title and copyright pages with the CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO licence, a contents list and abbreviations. It then explains how the data table should be read, including how dates of wild and vaccine-derived poliovirus circulation and of oral polio vaccine use were recorded. Notes clarify which samples count as potentially infectious material for each virus type, and that the month of last trivalent OPV use was set to December where only the year was known.

summary.text: Table A2.1 lists, country by country from Afghanistan onwards, the periods when materials collected there may be potentially infectious for wild or circulating vaccine-derived polioviruses of types 1, 2 and 3. A further column gives the periods when samples may contain type 2 oral polio vaccine or Sabin2-related virus, which must be mitigated, while types 2 and 3 must be contained now. Footnotes explain special cases and territories listed under other countries. The table is followed by a long reference list of surveillance reports and studies on poliovirus circulation.
